chapter: Los Angeles scene and the Ellington sound
title: Los Angeles ballrooms and small clubs
summary: He describes Solomon's with three bands, Cinderella Roof, mostly small clubs and few after-hours spots with music.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: What nightspots were there then? There was the Cotton Club and there was teh Apex, and what else?
Apex. Oh, there were many -- there were several bands employed at the Solomon's Ballroom, and all of these dance palaces up and down the avenues. Oh, there were many bands in existence.
Where was Solomon's?

Solomon's was down on 9th and Grand. It was a huge place. It had three bands, the two in the end of the hall, one band at each end of the hall, and then the feature band was set up in the middle of the hall. It was a great big hall, almost a block long.
Did they play alternatingly, or was it
Simultaneous? Alternating no, alternating.
Alternate.
I don't mean alternating dates, but they played --
Yeah, the same evening.
-- three times a night, you know, each band had three sessions.
Were there -- there were other ballrooms, you said, do you remember --
Oh yes.
-- what they were?
Cinderella Roof, oh, there were --
Where was that?
That was around 7th Street, I think, and out near Westlake, and over in that area.
And clubs, were there small clubs, or --
Many small --
-- any other large clubs?
Mostly small clubs. Not too large. Of course there were places like the Ambassador and places like that. Clubs came and went. They didn't stay. Only a few of them stayed very long.
How about after-hours clubs? Was there

Not too much, no. There were mostly record players, and after hours there were many after-hour spots which featured late suppers and different food places, and of course drinking, but not too much music. It was either Victrola or something like that. Not too many of them had groups. If they did they were two and three and four-piece, that's all.
